item.title: Georgia marks a year of protests
item.description: Despite declining numbers, hundreds — sometimes thousands — continue to protest daily. The duration of the movement remains uncertain, but the government’s shift toward authoritarianism appears unmistakable.

item.title: ‘Identity is never fixed. It’s layered, constantly shifting’: An interview with Iranian-American artist Soraya Sharghi
item.description: “My way of resisting is through creating by bringing beauty, strength, and imagination into spaces where control or limitation once existed.”

item.title: Healing the past to strengthen the future: Why the Caribbean needs to talk about ancestral trauma
item.description: “What our grandparents practised instinctively through prayer, song, and time spent in the natural world, neuroscience is now validating with brain scans and data.”

item.title: Healing through music: Defying silence in Myanmar
item.description: "“To me, being a feminist means kindness. If I stay silent when others suffer, one day it will be my turn to suffer too."

item.title: Brazilians take to the streets calling attention to a crisis of violence against women
item.description: In 2024, Brazil had 1,492 victims of femicide, the highest number registered since the femicide law came into effect. This represents four women killed every day for reasons linked to their gender.

item.title: Green dignity and public visibility: GIA’s intersectional approach to transgender rights and climate justice in Pakistan
item.description: Global Voices spoke with the Gender Interactive Alliance (GIA) about their work and how it connects with COP30’s focus on justice, human rights, and a circular economy.

item.title: Armenia and Azerbaijan: dialogue or performance?
item.description: Armenia and Azerbaijan, after the second Karabakh war, appear increasingly close to normalizing relations, but analysts and activists are not entirely convinced that the process will be transparent and inclusive.

item.title: Why cybersafety matters in the African Union–European Union partnership
item.description: Research shows that women are less likely to access the Internet than men and face higher exposure to harassment once they are online. These conditions limit participation and restrict leadership.

item.title: What China’s energy sector can and cannot do for the Global South
item.description: Will South Asia’s energy future be determined by local needs or by the strategic interests of a rising great power?

item.title: What’s behind the growing anti-immigrant discourse around stateless Rohingya in India
item.description: The “Bangladeshi Rohingya” framing has become a central weapon in anti-immigrant narratives through systematic disinformation campaigns in India’s digital sphere.
